newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Speaker backs Israel on military action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Speaker backs Israel on military action.

text.p: Republican Speaker Newt Gingrich, one of America's most powerful politicians, gave Israel his backing on Sunday to take military action against Palestinian militants and said the United States needed a "tougher anti-terrorist strategy."

As Israel braced for the possibility of more suicide bomb attacks ahead of a Sunday deadline by Islamist militant group Hamas, Gingrich directed fierce condemnation at Yasser Arafat and the Palestinian Authority.

Speaking on Fox Television's "Fox News Sunday" programme, the House of Representatives speaker said Israel had the right to take whatever measures it saw fit to protect its citizens from the atrocities of last week's suicide bomb attacks.
"Israelis have every right to protect themselves, they have every right to go after Hamas," he said.

"The United States should come down firmly on the side of protecting innocent citizens and opposing terrorism and flatly let it be known in the Middle East that we will be supportive of steps needed to protect innocent Israelis."

Thirteen Israelis were killed by two suicide bombers in a Jerusalem marketplace on Wednesday and Israeli police fear more violence after Hamas issued an ultimatum that Israel release all political prisoners by 9 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) Sunday.
Gingrich said he backed whatever steps Israel needed to impose to protect its citizens.

"If that includes raids into Palestinian territory, if that includes arresting some of the Palestinian Authority leaders who themselves have engaged in terrorist acts, whatever steps have to be taken ought to be taken and the Palestinian Authority should know it's only going to survive within a framework of security," he said.
He criticised Palestinian President Arafat for not doing enough to crack down on militants and said Arafat had lost all credibility in the U.S. Congress as a leader.

"The clear evidence that Yasser Arafat and the Palestinian Authority have not only not stopped terrorism, but had people in their organisation helping terrorists, the fact that Israelis have been dying and the very fact that Hamas is as bold as it is in new statements, indicates the U.S. needs to be prepared with a new and tougher anti-terrorist strategy for the Middle East," he said.
"The (Clinton) administration is very concerned about what happened and the growing sense of the administration is that the Palestinian Authority is not doing its job," he added.
"Arafat has squandered what was a great opportunity to build genuine peace in the region and now the question is where do we go from here."

Israel suspended already dormant peace talks with the Palestinians after the bombing, sealed the West Bank and Gaza Strip, and arrested 116 Palestinians suspected of involvement in Islamic militant groups.

Palestinians accused Israel of imposing collective punishment on Palestinians and expressed hope U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, due later this week on another mediation mission, could put peacemaking back on track.
